_meta.what: HAND-AUTHORED metric trees for the nine photo-derived meshes. Written by a person reading proportions off a 24-unit grid laid over orthographic renders of each mesh. NOTHING here was produced by, checked against, or tuned toward any extraction pipeline.
_meta.not_compiled: These trees have NOT been run through TreeMaker. Nobody knows whether they pack. Several faithful variants exceed MAX_LEAVES=8 and certainly will not. Treat 'packable' as 'inside the leaf-count window', which is a necessary condition and not a sufficient one.
_meta.reference: Structure follows COrigami's stick figures (~/Desktop/origami_samples): a body spine of internal nodes, multi-segment limbs with named joints, integer edge lengths on a stated grid.
_meta.frame: +x forward (toward the head), +y up, +z to the animal's LEFT. Directions are drawing hints; the tree is (parent, length) and directions never affect it.
_meta.edge_naming: An edge is named for the node it ENTERS. `hock_l: 4` is the segment ending at the left hock.
_meta.length_units: `length_grid` is the authored integer. `length` in tree_nodes is scaled so the longest edge in that tree is 0.40, matching mesh_to_tree.LONGEST_LIMB_TARGET.

variants.faithful: COrigami's convention, which gives ears, crests and pedipalps their own leaves.
variants.packable: This repo's convention (fixtures/anatomy_expectation.json): one leaf per terminal appendage, sub-flap detail excluded, and never more than MAX_LEAVES=8.

dog.how_measured: side view: withers x7, hip x16, ground y21.5, nose x1, tail base x17.5 curling to a tip at (20, 2.5). Foreleg 12 units shoulder to ground, hind leg 11.
dog.node_order_rationale: quadruped order: hubs and legs first, head and tail LAST -- body_plans.py records that as the measured-to-pack ordering, and the engine seeds placement from list position
merges_faithful_to_packable: ear_tip_l + ear_tip_r -> head_base (sub-flap detail under the repo convention; COrigami would keep them, and the jerboa does)

cat.how_measured: side view: nose x22.5, shoulders x17, hips x7, ground y19.5. Tail base (5,9) curling left to (1,9.5); measured along the curl, not the chord, so 7 rather than 4.
cat.node_order_rationale: quadruped order: hubs and legs first, head and tail LAST -- body_plans.py records that as the measured-to-pack ordering, and the engine seeds placement from list position
cat.caveat: The mesh carries a thin whisker sheet across the muzzle and a stray plane spanning the flank -- the source of its 38 bodies. Neither is anatomy and neither is in this tree.

horse.how_measured: side view: muzzle x21, poll x17.5, withers x13, croup x4.5, ground y18. The long neck (5) against the dog's (2) is the single biggest proportional difference between the two quadrupeds. Legs read at four different phases of a trot and are authored EQUAL: a metric tree carries proportion, not pose.
horse.node_order_rationale: quadruped order: hubs and legs first, head and tail LAST -- body_plans.py records that as the measured-to-pack ordering, and the engine seeds placement from list position

lizard.how_measured: top view: snout x22, shoulders x17, hips x9.5, tail tip x1. Limbs SPRAWL -- they leave the body sideways before turning down, which is why the elbow/knee directions carry a large z and the shoulder-to-foot path (5) is longer than the straight-line distance (4).
lizard.node_order_rationale: quadruped order: hubs and legs first, head and tail LAST -- body_plans.py records that as the measured-to-pack ordering, and the engine seeds placement from list position
lizard.identical_note: COrigami fidelity and the packable window AGREE here at 6 leaves, so the two trees are the same object. A lizard has no ear or crest flap to spend, and its five-toed feet are sub-flap detail under BOTH conventions -- COrigami's jerboa terminates a limb at one toe node, not five.
lizard.caveat: This mesh is a flattened plaque: extents 1.961 x 0.318 x 1.027, aspect 6.2, because the photograph is a low, near-top-down view of an animal lying on a rock. The tree is authored from the animal's proportions as read in TOP view, which is the view that survives.

frog.how_measured: side view: snout x17.5, body_c x9, rump x4, ground y17. The hind limb is the whole story: 4+4+3 = 11 units of limb folded into 7 units of body length, thigh pointing BACK, shank forward-down, foot forward again. Forelimb totals 6.
frog.node_order_rationale: head LAST; there is no tail to place after it
frog.identical_note: Identical at 5 leaves. An adult anuran has no tail (order Anura, 'without tail') and no ear or crest flap, so COrigami fidelity buys nothing the window cannot hold.
frog.caveat: The extractor read 12-42 leaves on this mesh at every one of 24 search cells and never entered the 4..8 window. The long digits are why. They are sub-flap detail here and cost 0 leaves -- the gap between 5 and 42 is the gap between a designer and a skeletoniser, not between two meshes.

bird.how_measured: side view: beak tip x0.5, head_base x4, body_c x8, tail base x11, tail tip x20.5 -- the tail is 10 units, longer than the bird's own body. Legs are short (3). Wing length 7 read off the folded wing's SEAM on the body surface, since the wings are not separate geometry.
bird.node_order_rationale: wings and legs before the head chain; tail LAST
merges_faithful_to_packable: crest_tip -> head_base (a crest is sub-flap detail under the repo convention; COrigami keeps such things, cf. the hoopoe's fanned crest and the peacock's tail fan)
bird.caveat: TWO things in this mesh are not in this tree. The PERCH lifted with the bird -- background removal kept the stump under its feet -- and it is scenery, not anatomy. And the WINGS are fused to the body, so no extractor can find them; a human can, because a human knows a blue jay has wings. That is the clearest case in this set of hand-authoring recovering what extraction structurally cannot.

starfish.how_measured: face-on view: disc centred (11,12) with radius 3; the five arm tips sit at (11.5,0.5) (0.5,11) (21.5,9.5) (17.5,21.5) (5.5,21.5), all 10.5-11.6 units from centre. Authored equal at 11 = 5 + 6.
starfish.node_order_rationale: arm0 (the axial arm) FIRST, then the two mirror pairs outward, so the axis is seeded before the paired flaps
starfish.identical_note: Identical at 5 leaves. Every leaf is an arm; there is no head and no tail to add or drop, so the two conventions cannot disagree.
starfish.symmetry_note: arm0 is axial and UNPAIRED by construction. Do not read its lack of a partner as a lost mirror twin -- odd radial symmetry cannot pair every ray.

contract_warnings: the root has 5 children. This is NOT a predicted failure: a k-child root (a star) is measured packing 3/3 at equal lengths for k=4, 5, 6 and 8, and only k=7 fails there (fixtures/s5_engine_repair_evidence.json, packability_control). Grouping flaps onto 2-3 hubs is still the layout the four body-plan templates use and the one the rescue ladder has the most levers for.

spider.how_measured: top view: cephalothorax (13,11), abdomen centre (7,11), abdomen tip x3. Leg tips read 8 to 11.4 units from the cephalothorax; legs I and IV are longest, II and III shortest, which is the real arachnid pattern and is preserved rather than averaged. Each leg rises at the femur and descends through tibia and tarsus.
spider.node_order_rationale: legs in pairs front to back, then the abdomen chain; the cephalothorax roots the tree because every leg attaches there
merges_faithful_to_packable: palp_l + palp_r -> cephalothorax (pedipalps are sub-flap detail under the repo convention, which excludes antennae and the like)

abdomen DEMOTED from flap to trunk: 8 legs + abdomen = 9 exceeds MAX_LEAVES=8 and no eighth leg can be deleted without deleting real anatomy, so the opisthosoma stops being a flap and becomes the body the legs radiate from. This is the ONLY subject where the window costs a feature the anatomy oracle counts.

octopus.how_measured: top view: arm crown (11,11), mantle running back to a tip at x20, so the mantle is 9 units. Arm tips read 10 to 14 units from the crown, the front pair longest -- the arms are NOT equal and are not authored equal.
octopus.node_order_rationale: arms in mirror pairs front to back, then the mantle chain
merges_faithful_to_packable: mantle DEMOTED from flap to trunk: 8 arms + mantle = 9 exceeds MAX_LEAVES=8. Same trade as the spider's abdomen, and the same reasoning -- an arm is not deletable, the axial mass is.
octopus.symmetry_note: Eight arms about ONE bilateral plane give 4 clean pairs. This is the one radial subject whose symmetry is even, so unlike the starfish nothing is left unpaired.
